facts.statement: Selmasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically from the Santonian to the Campanian stages.
The genus Selmasaurus was officially described by Wright and Shannon in 1988.
A nearly complete Selmasaurus skull and partial skeleton were discovered by Steve Johnson and his family in 1996.
facts.quote: A remarkably well preserved and nearly complete Selmasaurus skull and partial postcranial skeleton was discovered by Steve Johnson and family in 1996

facts.statement: Selmasaurus is classified within the Plioplatecarpinae subfamily, alongside genera such as Angolasaurus and Platecarpus.
facts.quote: It is classified as part of the Plioplatecarpinae subfamily alongside genera like Angolasaurus and Platecarpus.

facts.statement: Selmasaurus is unique among mosasaurs for having an unusually akinetic skull that cannot widen to swallow large prey.
facts.quote: Selmasaurus is unique among the mosasaurs in that its skull is unusually akinetic, meaning that it is incapable of widening to swallow larger prey.

facts.statement: Selmasaurus was a small predatory mosasaur reaching approximately 3 to 5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Selmasaurus was a small predatory mosasaur at approximately 3–5 meters in length.

facts.statement: Wright and Shannon classified Selmasaurus as a member of the mosasaur subfamily Plioplatecarpinae.
facts.quote: Wright and Shannon classified Selmasaurus as a member of the mosasaur subfamily Plioplatecarpinae

facts.statement: Stable isotope analysis indicates that S. johnsoni was one of the few plioplatecarpines not restricted to nearshore marine environments.
facts.quote: According to stable isotope analysis, S. johnsoni was one of the few plioplatecarpines that was not restricted to nearshore marine environments.

facts.statement: In 1998, Caitlín R. Kiernan identified calcareous nanoplankton in the holotype specimen, indicating it originated from basal Campanian beds in the Mooreville Chalk Formation.
facts.quote: Then in 1998, Caitlín R. Kiernan extracted chalky matrix from the basilar canal of the basioccipital and identified calcareous nanoplankton that indicated GSATC 221 had originated from basal Campanian beds within the lower unnamed member of the Mooreville Chalk Formation (Selma Group).

facts.statement: The specimen of S. johnsoni was found in the Santonian or Campanian marine horizon of the Niobrara Formation in western Kansas.
facts.quote: A remarkably well preserved and nearly complete Selmasaurus skull and partial postcranial skeleton was discovered by Steve Johnson and family in 1996, from the Santonian or Campanian marine horizon in the Niobrara Formation of Niobrara Chalk, western Kansas.

facts.statement: Longrich et al. (2024) recovered Selmasaurus within a monophyletic clade of non-plioplatecarpine plioplatecarpine mosasaurids based on phylogenetic analyses.
facts.quote: In their 2024 description of the Moroccan plioplatecarpine Khinjaria, Longrich et al. used phylogenetic analyses to recover it within a monophyletic clade of non-plioplatecarpin plioplatecarpine mosasaurids.
